content: Title 21 of the United States Code is a section of federal law that regulates food and drugs. It is organized into 25 distinct chapters, each addressing specific areas of regulation and oversight. Below is a detailed explanation of the chapters: 1. Adulterated or Misbranded Foods or Drugs: 2. Teas (Repealed): This chapter previously addressed regulations related to teas but has since been repealed. 3. Filled Milk: This chapter governs the production and sale of filled milk, which is milk that has been modified by adding fats or oils other than milk fat. 4. Animals, Meats, and Meat and Dairy Products: 5. Viruses, Serums, Toxins, Antitoxins, and Analogous Products: This chapter regulates biological products such as vaccines, serums, and antitoxins, ensuring their safety, efficacy, and proper manufacturing practices. 6. Bureau of Narcotics (Omitted): This chapter previously addressed the Bureau of Narcotics but has been omitted from the current code. 7. Narcotic Drugs (Repealed or Transferred): This chapter dealt with narcotic drugs, but its provisions have been repealed or transferred to other sections. 8. Practice of Pharmacy and Sale of Poisons in Consular Districts in China: This chapter historically regulated the practice of pharmacy and the sale of poisons in U.S. consular districts in China. 9. Narcotic Farms: This chapter pertains to the establishment and operation of narcotic farms, which were facilities for the treatment and rehabilitation of individuals addicted to narcotics. 10. Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act: This chapter contains the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, which provides comprehensive regulations for the safety, labeling, and marketing of food, drugs, and cosmetics. 11. Poultry and Poultry Products Inspection: 12. Manufacture of Narcotic Drugs (Repealed): This chapter previously regulated the manufacturing of narcotic drugs but has been repealed. 13. Meat Inspection: 14. Drug Abuse Prevention and Control: 15. Alcohol and Drug Abuse Educational Programs and Activities: This chapter promotes educational programs and activities aimed at preventing alcohol and drug abuse. 16. Egg Products Inspection: 17. Drug Abuse Prevention, Treatment, and Rehabilitation: This chapter focuses on programs and initiatives for the prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of individuals affected by drug abuse. 18. National Drug Enforcement Policy (Repealed): This chapter previously outlined national drug enforcement policies but has been repealed. 19. President’s Media Commission on Alcohol and Drug Abuse Prevention: This chapter involves the establishment of a media commission to promote awareness and prevention of alcohol and drug abuse. 20. Pesticide Monitoring Improvements: This chapter addresses improvements in the monitoring and regulation of pesticide use to protect public health. 21. National Drug Control Program: This chapter outlines the framework for the national drug control program, which coordinates efforts to combat drug abuse and trafficking. 22. Biomaterials Access Assurance: 23. National Drug Control Policy: This chapter establishes policies and strategies for national drug control efforts. 24. National Youth Anti-Drug Media Campaign: This chapter focuses on media campaigns aimed at preventing drug use among youth. 25. International Narcotics Trafficking: This chapter addresses efforts to combat international narcotics trafficking and its impact on the United States. Chapter 13: Controlled Substances Act This chapter includes the Controlled Substances Act, which is part of the Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act of 1970. It provides the legal framework for regulating the manufacture, distribution, and use of controlled substances, including their classification into schedules based on their potential for abuse and medical utility.
